meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Egypt (unitary national jurisdiction; no sub-federal tax or incorporation distinction)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Napoleonic statutory tradition) with Islamic Sharia as a principal source of legislation under Article 2 of the Constitution of 2014; unitary jurisdiction
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Bilateral Investment Treaty between Egypt and the People's Republic of China (in force since 1996)
Agreement on Promotion and Reciprocal Protection of Investments between Egypt and the United Arab Emirates (in force)
Treaty between Egypt and the United States of America concerning the Encouragement and Reciprocal Protection of Investments (in force since 1992)
Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement between Egypt and the United Kingdom (in force)
Euro-Mediterranean Association Agreement between Egypt and the European Union (signed 2001, in force 2004)
Greater Arab Free Trade Area (GAFTA) and COMESA preferential trade instruments binding Egypt

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law No. 80 of 2002 on Combating Money Laundering and the Financing of Terrorism, as amended by Law No. 36 of 2014 and Law No. 154 of 2019; Executive Regulations issued by Prime Ministerial Decree No. 949 of 2003, as amended; beneficial-owner identification and reporting obligations under Article 15 of Law No. 80 of 2002, Ministry of Justice implementing decrees and the directives of the Egyptian Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating Unit (MLTFCU); Companies Law No. 159 of 1981, as amended; Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 and its Executive Regulations (GAFI UBO declaration filings); Central Bank of Egypt AML/CFT instructions applicable to DNFBPs and retail payment service providers.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport authority or notary public in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (legalization by the Egyptian Embassy or Consulate in the issuing country, followed by authentication by the Egyptian Ministry of Foreign Affairs)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation, Certificate of Good Standing or equivalent commercial register extract of each foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent companies registry or chamber of commerce of the shareholder's jurisdiction of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (Egyptian Embassy or Consulate legalization, then Egyptian Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and verification of source of funds for the intended incorporation capital
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (Egyptian Embassy or Consulate legalization, then Egyptian Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of No Criminal Record (police clearance) for each proposed manager, incorporator and local representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ministry of Interior or competent judicial authority of the person's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (Egyptian Embassy or Consulate legalization, then Egyptian Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney appointing the Egyptian incorporation agent and notarized draft of the Arabic Articles of Association (contract of formation)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the document's country of origin; Egyptian Notary Office (Ministry of Justice) for the Arabic counterpart
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (Egyptian Embassy or Consulate legalization, then Egyptian Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all incorporators, shareholders, directors, authorized signatories and ultimate beneficial owners against the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, the OFAC SDN and Consolidated non-SDN lists, EU and UK sanctions, and the domestic counter-terrorism and PEP databases maintained by the Egyptian Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating Unit (MLTFCU) and the Central Bank of Egypt. PEP status is assessed under the FATF-aligned Egyptian definition, including family members and close associates. Any sanctions hit, PEP flag, or material red flag triggers enhanced due diligence, beneficial-ownership re-verification, and mandatory filing of a suspicious transaction report. All screening results must be archived in the AML/CFT compliance file and made available to the MLTFCU upon request under Law No. 80 of 2002.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) Investor Services Center, including the electronic name reservation module (www.investinegypt.gov.eg); followed by registration in the Commercial Register maintained by the Ministry of Trade and Industry.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The legal corporate name must be in Arabic under Law No. 159 of 1981; a transliterated or English-language trading name may be recorded as a secondary commercial name, but the Arabic name is the controlling legal identity. The name must correspond to the licensed retail food and grocery activity (supermarket), must not duplicate or be confusingly similar to any existing registered mark or company name, and must follow GAFI and Commercial Registry naming conventions, including the standard Arabic form of 'name + activity description' (for example, 'Asian Supermarket for Foodstuffs').
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon refusal the registrar issues a written reasoned decision. The applicant may submit an administrative objection to the GAFI Legal Affairs Sector within 15 business days of notification, attaching alternative name variants. If the objection is denied, the applicant may appeal to the competent Administrative Court of the State Council (Conseil d'État) within 60 days, or resubmit a modified name through the GAFI electronic portal. The reservation holds for 30 days and is renewable only while the incorporation dossier remains pending before GAFI.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not acceptable for the licensed retail grocery activity (ISIC 4721). The municipal commercial license and the registered office requirement mandate a fixed, habitable commercial premises in Egypt evidenced by a ratified lease contract; virtual or 'smart' offices do not satisfy the physical-store or licensed-address requirement, although a virtual correspondence address may supplement the registered office.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High: estimated 75-85% probability of at least one unannounced physical inspection within the first 12 months of licensing by the municipal health and supply authorities, civil defense, the tax administration and the commercial registry; retail food premises must maintain statutory books and records at the licensed address.

LLC incorporation registration fee at the GAFI one-stop shop

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for fixed-scope incorporation engagement

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law No. 159 of 2003 on Joint-Stock Companies, Partnerships Limited by Shares, and Limited Liability Companies, as amended by Law No. 149 of 2022 (Company and Small Enterprise Law); Investment Law No. 72 of 2017, and its Executive Regulations
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) One-Stop Shop and the Governorate Commercial Registry, Ministry of Trade and Industry
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Incorporation Contract (Aqd al-Taasis) filed for issuance of the Commercial Registry Certificate (al-Sijill al-Tijari)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum stated capital under Law No. 159/2003 as amended; the stated capital must be fully subscribed by the partners, with the paid-up portion deposited in a temporary bank account opened with a CBE-licensed bank and blocked until the Commercial Registry Certificate is issued, as evidenced by a bank capital deposit certificate
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: In accordance with Law No. 159 of 2003 (as amended), the subscribers holding the entire share capital adopt this First Board/Managers Resolution: (1) the share capital declared in the Incorporation Contract is subscribed in full; (2) the registered office is established at the address stated in the contract within the Cairo Commercial Registry area; (3) the persons named in Appendix A are appointed managers vested with full legal powers of representation; (4) each manager is individually authorized to deposit the capital in a temporary bank account, to file the incorporation instruments with GAFI and the Commercial Registry, and to obtain the commercial registration and tax cards; (5) this resolution remains effective until amended by the partners.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI Online One-Stop Shop - Name Clearance Section
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an electronic name clearance application with three proposed Arabic names and a transliterated Latin commercial name in the order of preference. The GAFI system automatically screens against existing trade names and reserves the approved name for 60 days. Foreign founders must attach a notarized consent to use the name in Arabic.
required_dossiers: signed name clearance application form
copy of each founder's passport or national ID
board resolution or founder consent to name selection
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: File a written appeal with the Name Clearance Committee or immediately resubmit three new alternative name variants; name reservation fees are retained and a new filing is required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public Office operating within the GAFI Center, Cairo, or the competent Governorate Notary Department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the Arabic-language Incorporation Contract before the Notary Public. All subscribers or their duly authorized attorneys must appear in person or by notarized power of attorney. The notary shall legalize signatures, certify the legal capacity of each subscriber, and retain the authenticated original for the Commercial Registry file.
required_dossiers: draft Incorporation Contract in Arabic (original and 2 copies)
passport or national ID of every subscriber
notarized power of attorney for any signatory acting on behalf of a shareholder
name clearance certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary queries any clause for inconsistency with mandatory provisions of Law No. 159/2003, the subscribers must sign a supplementary correction page and re-notarize without reopening the full articles.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit of Share Capital in Temporary Bank Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CBE-licensed commercial bank (e.g., National Bank of Egypt, Banque Misr) selected by the founders
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary account in the name of the company 'in formation' using the reserved name. Deposit the full subscribed paid-up capital and obtain a Capital Deposit Certificate in Arabic and English detailing the amount and blocking condition. The funds remain frozen until presentation of the Commercial Registry Certificate; the bank releases the balance thereafter for lawful corporate expenses.
required_dossiers: notarized Incorporation Contract
founder identification documents and bank KYC forms
proof of name reservation
company formation checklist issued by the bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank rejects the deposit instruction due to insufficient capital subscription, the shareholders must execute a supplementary subscription resolution, increase or confirm the paid-up amount, and obtain a revised Capital Deposit Certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Registry Application and Certificate Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop Commercial Registry counters and the Governorate Commercial Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarized Incorporation Contract, Capital Deposit Certificate, and appointment resolutions at the GAFI One-Stop Shop. Pay the statutory filing and stamp fees by e-payment. The registry verifies the legality of the clauses, the address of the registered office, and the legality of manager appointments, then issues the Commercial Registry Certificate bearing the company registration number and legal form.
required_dossiers: notarized Incorporation Contract (original plus 2 certified copies)
Capital Deposit Certificate
proof of name clearance
consent letters of appointed managers and their criminal record extracts
lease contract or title evidence of the registered office
payment receipts for fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to the Registry's written query within 15 working days by submitting a formal memorandum; if the objection concerns the articles, amend by a complementary resolution and re-file the corrected contract.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration and VAT Code to Enable Import and Sales
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) registration offices and the GAFI One-Stop Shop tax window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Commercial Registry Certificate to obtain the Tax Card containing the Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN), register for Value Added Tax (import of Asian condiments will activate the import customs linkage), and open the electronic invoicing account in the ETA portal. This step is mandatory before placing import orders through the customs code.
required_dossiers: Commercial Registry Certificate
notarized Incorporation Contract
valid managers' IDs and residence addresses
registered office lease agreement
bank statement of the corporate account or Capital Deposit Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax officer queries the tax card application, submit the correction file within 30 days; for late VAT registration, file a written waiver request supported by evidence of turnover below EGP 500,000 until the first 12 months end.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of Formation Extract and Beneficial Ownership Filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI Corporate Registration Department and the Official Gazette / two daily newspapers designated for legal notices
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Publish the statutory formation summary in two daily Egyptian newspapers or through the official electronic gazette. Deliver the publication slip to the Commercial Registry within the statutory deadline and file the Beneficial Ownership (UBO) declaration and Economic Activity Data form to close the formation file and activate the electronic seal for registrations.
required_dossiers: publication proof from the two newspapers or the electronic gazette
Beneficial Ownership Declaration form signed by the legal representative
Commercial Registry Certificate copy
copy of the managers' resolution approving the publication text
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the publication contains a clerical variance from the registered articles, publish a corrective notice at the company's expense and confirm the correction before the Commercial Registry.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Governorate Municipal Licensing Department (Ministry of Local Development) and the Egyptian National Food Safety Authority (NFSA) for food business registration
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal Commercial License for Supermarket Retailing (Rokhsat al-Mahalla) and NFSA Food Safety Registration Certificate

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B - Simplified Environmental Registration and Environmental Review under Law No. 4/1994; a Full EIA Report is not required for retail grocery premises with total refrigeration load up to 250 kW and no industrial effluent lines
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater to public sewer: BOD ≤ 60 mg/L, COD ≤ 130 mg/L, TSS ≤ 80 mg/L, total grease ≤ 15 mg/L per Cabinet Decree No. 44/2000 and Law No. 93/1962; refrigeration systems must be CFC-free and leak-tested under Montreal Protocol standards; indoor ambient CO ≤ 10 ppm and VOC-controlled to workplace limits under Labor Law No. 12/2003; solid waste must be segregated for transport by approved municipal or licensed waste carriers

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Civil Defense (Fire Engineering) approval from the Ministry of Interior covering fire exits, extinguishers, automatic alarm and evacuation signage; structural load verification of racking and cold-room installations by the Governorate Engineering Office; occupational health and safety clearance from the Ministry of Manpower including a first-aid room, workforce injury insurance, sanitation and ventilation standards under Law No. 12/2003.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) – official e-portal at https://www.eta.gov.eg for tax card, VAT registration, e-invoicing, and e-receipts
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Egyptian LLC must obtain a Tax Card (TIN) by registering with the Egyptian Tax Authority using the company commercial registry extract, lease/power-of-attorney, board resolution, and financial statements. VAT registration is mandatory if annual taxable turnover exceeds EGP 500,000; application is filed online through the ETA portal, followed by issuance of a VAT certificate and activation of the e-invoice account.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Egypt does not maintain check-the-box classification for LLCs; an Egyptian LLC is per se a resident corporation taxed at entity level. Election available: consolidated tax group filing among Egyptian resident companies under the Egyptian Income Tax Law; free-zone entities may elect tax-exempt/tax-holiday regime under Law No. 83/2002 read with the Suez Canal Economic Zone regulations; no hybrid mismatch elections exist under Egyptian domestic law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 (annual taxable supplies by any person performing a taxable activity in Egypt; threshold applies to goods and services)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory real-time e-invoicing and e-receipts through ETA's e-invoice portal. All VAT-registered taxpayers must integrate their billing systems with the ETA API for immediate clearance of each invoice; invoice data is digitally signed, stamped with a QR code, and validated in real time before issuance to buyers. Non-compliance blocks issuance and triggers automated penalty assessment.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available for export of tangible goods outside Egypt evidenced by customs export entry, and for offshore services supplied to non-residents with economic use outside Egypt. The exporter must hold a valid VAT registration certificate and an exporter code issued by the General Authority for Export and Import Control; goods must physically leave Egypt within the legally prescribed timeframes.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (ACID). Bill of Lading / Airway Bill. Inward Remittance Certificate evidencing receipt of export proceeds in foreign currency. Bank debit/credit advice and FX repatriation proof. Copy of the export VAT zero-rating invoice. Certificate of Origin where required.
Supplier/registration copies evidencing VAT ID and exporter code.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The ETA may deny zero-rating and recover VAT at 14% plus interest from the date of supply if the export documentation is incomplete or inconsistent; fraudulent zero-rating claims expose the taxpayer to administrative penalties up to 100% of the tax evaded, daily late payment penalties (usually 2% per month for the understated VAT), criminal prosecution, and possible customs and foreign-exchange penalties. ETA and the Central Bank of Egypt also cross-check export invoices against inward remittance bank records, triggering clawback for uncollected export proceeds within the 180-day deadline.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) - Foreign Exchange Department, acting with the CBE Anti-Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Unit (AMLFU) and the Egyptian Customs Authority (ACID platform) for trade-linked foreign exchange control enforcement.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Egypt operates a unified managed-floating exchange rate regime following the 5-6 March 2024 liberalisation under an IMF Extended Fund Facility; the interbank USD/EGP market determines the official price and the pound is current-account convertible. Trade payments, service fees, royalties, dividends, and branch profit remittances are transferable through authorised dealing banks (AD banks) upon presentation of underlying contracts, commercial invoices, customs ACID declarations, and proof of tax settlement. Capital-account openness is partial: inbound foreign direct investment (FDI) is welcomed and must be registered in a CBE Investment Registration File (IRF), while repatriation of registered FDI principal, liquidation proceeds, and dividends is permitted only with audited financials and a Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) clearance. Practical remittance hurdles for a grocery-retail LLC include hard-currency liquidity cycles, bank-side EGP conversion requirements for local expenses, and documentary duplication across Customs, ETA, and CBE forms. Portfolio outflows and resident outward capital transfers remain prohibited or strictly conditioned on CBE approval.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under CBE foreign-exchange circulars read with Unified Banking Law No. 194 of 2020 (Arts. 91-94), an exporter must transfer the full gross export proceeds to its account maintained with an authorized bank in Egypt no later than 90 days from the bill-of-lading date for merchandise exports, extendable to 180 days for documented deferred-payment trade. Since the November 2016 FX liberalisation, no fixed mandatory conversion ratio into EGP is imposed on general merchandise exporters: 100% of the hard-currency proceeds may be retained in the exporter's foreign-currency Export Proceeds Account provided the 90-day repatriation deadline is met. The CBE retains reserved powers to order conversion of a percentage of export receipts in a balance-of-payments emergency or for exports settled under bilateral non-convertible-currency agreements. Non-repatriation is an exchange-control violation attracting criminal sanctions, fines, and bank-relationship termination under Law 194/2020 rather than a mere tax default.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow / Investment Registration File (IRF) account plus multi-currency operational current account (EGP and USD) with SWIFT corporate e-banking
Operational current account (EGP and USD) with Export Proceeds / Import Settlement sub-accounts
Operational current account with trade finance desk for LC issuance and documentary collections under a 100% cash-cover model for new LLCs
Operational account with import collections and letters of credit supported by parent-group trade finance review

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: LOW as a primary treasury rail, MEDIUM-AUXILIARY only for incidental low-value refunds or petty disbursements. Egypt does not authorise offshore cross-border electronic money institutions (EMIs) as bank counterparties; the CBE, under Law 194/2020 and the AMLFU AML framework, licenses domestic payment service providers (Meeza-branded neopay firms and a small set of fintechs) that cannot clear SWIFT MT103 corporate import flows on a standalone basis. Offshore EMIs (Wise, Revolut Business, Payoneer) may not hold EGP balances, are not admitted to Egyptian ACH or RTGS clearings, and inbound USD received from such EMIs is treated as a third-party transfer requiring full invoice and CBE form support. Reliance on an offshore EMI as the corporate settlement account would frustrate CBE import settlement registration, ACID customs declarations, and IRF reconciliation, and is therefore legally and operationally non-viable as the main clearing channel.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A physical or live hybrid interview is mandatory in substance. Under CBE KYC rules and Unified Banking Law 194/2020 Art. 71, the Egyptian-resident manager or legal representative must appear in person before the relationship officer or a CBE-licensed agent; each signatory, director, and every beneficial owner (natural person holding 25% or the ultimate controlling chain) must present original passport or national ID plus a board resolution signed by the shareholders. Remote video-KYC is generally not accepted for foreign signatories; a consular-legalised or apostilled power of attorney may represent a non-resident minority shareholder, but the resident manager must still attend the onboarding interview. Practical consequence: foreign shareholders should either travel to Cairo for the account-opening session or formally appoint the resident operating manager as sole local representative with full signatory authority.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque non-resident UBO chain: foreign Asian shareholders registered in an intermediate jurisdiction (for example Hong Kong, Singapore, or UAE) without clear natural-person disclosure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled or consular-legalised certificates of incorporation and certificates of incumbency for every intermediate entity; full register of members traced to natural persons; passport copies of all UBOs; notarised source-of-wealth and source-of-funds declarations; banker's reference from the foreign entity's top-tier Asian bank; IFRS or local GAAP audited financial statements of each intermediate entity; and a signed shareholder representation confirming absence of undisclosed nominees.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cash-intensive retail profile with volume cash deposits and high-frequency card settlements flagged against anti-structuring and money-service-business typologies.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Forward business plan and sales/cash-share projections by product aisle; signed POS terminal acquiring agreement with a CBE-licensed acquirer; in-store cash-management standard operating procedure with daily banking-sweep policy; first-12-month transactional projections; lease agreement and commercial registration evidencing physical premises; in-store inventory control and CCTV commitments; and board resolution adopting the group's AML manual.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Immediately post-incorporation high-volume import letters of credit and documentary collections directed to Vietnam, China, and India suppliers before the first audited financial year.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Pro-forma and final commercial invoices; purchase contracts with Incoterms (CIF or C&F); freight bookings and forwarder transaction history; Egyptian Customs ACID advance declarations; certificates of origin and ISO/HACCP certifications for food-grade condiments and vegetables; Ministry of Health import permits for plant-based products; proof of shareholder net worth or comfort letter from a foreign parent; and a board undertaking to transmit all customs clearance documents to the settling bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, PEP, or negative-news hits in the Asian supply chain or beneficiary bank corridors (dealings with persons named on OFAC, EU, UN, or Egyptian CBE listings).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Pre-transaction screening reports confirming no match against OFAC SDN, EU, UN and CBE/EGY consolidated listings for counterparties, banks, vessels, and UBOs; group structure chart with country-risk matrix; tax residency certificates and economic-citizenship documents of all UBOs; negative-news search outputs with supporting records; supplier contractual compliance warranties that goods are not of restricted or designated origin; and bank attestation of independent second-line review.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol: (1) open a Capital Escrow / Investment Registration File (IRF) account at the lead AD bank (for example National Bank of Egypt, SWIFT BIC NBEGEGCX) designated exclusively for FDI equity; (2) the foreign shareholder wires funds via SWIFT MT103 with Field 70 reciting the IRF number and the narrative 'FDI equity injection - subscription of shares in EG_LLC', instructing the remitting bank to use USD as interbank value currency with all charges borne by the sender; (3) the beneficiary AD bank credits the Capital Escrow account, books a Capital Inward Transfer, issues the Investment Registration Credit Note, and electronically notifies the CBE foreign-exchange reporting system; (4) the portion required for local working capital is converted at the unified interbank USD/EGP rate into the operational EGP account against proof of incorporation and tax registration, while unutilised USD remains in the USD operational account. Future dividend and liquidation remittances will be permitted only up to the cumulative registered IRF balance, therefore the MOA filed with the Egyptian Commercial Registry should state the injected amount as paid-up capital and the contribution should be recorded in the ETA tax card.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Principal clearing rails for supplier payments: (i) SWIFT MT103 telegraphic transfer on open-account terms for small and high-frequency items such as condiments and packaged goods; (ii) direct documentary collections (D/P or D/A) through the AD bank for mid-value consignments; and (iii) commercial irrevocable letters of credit at sight, issued in USD by the AD bank, typically requiring 100% cash cover for a newly incorporated LLC. Mandatory conditions: filing of the Egyptian Customs ACID advance cargo declaration, CBE electronic import settlement registration (successor to the paper Form D import declaration), and presentment to the AD bank of the final commercial invoice, bill of lading or airway bill, packing list, insurance certificate, certificate of origin, and food-safety import permits for plant-origin products. The bank will debit the EGP/USD account only after full verification of the underlying trade documentation. Egyptian domestic instant-payment rails (IPS) are not applicable to cross-border USD or LC clearing but may be used for intra-Egypt settlement of customs duties, VAT, and logistics costs.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable USD/EGP outright forwards with tenors of 1 to 12 months written by the AD bank against documented committed import payables, subject to collateral or margin of 10-15% for new clients, with no speculative rollover beyond the underlying trade schedule.

USD/EGP foreign-exchange swaps with the AD bank for temporary conversion of retained export proceeds or USD import sinking funds into EGP working capital and subsequent clawback into USD at the same bank on a booked trade-flow basis.

Natural hedge structure utilising a designated USD Import Sinking Fund sourced from retained hard-currency sales and registered export proceeds, preserving an offset against future USD payables with zero speculative trading; exchange-traded options and offshore non-deliverable forwards referencing the EGP are not authorised instruments for onshore retail corporates under current CBE practice.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (ETA Form No. 1) with audited financial statements and tax reconciliations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) - General Tax Office for Corporate Activities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within four calendar months after the end of the tax year; for a 31 December fiscal year-end, no later than 30 April of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 2% per month of tax due, capped at 12% for six months, plus monthly delay interest at 1.5% on the outstanding tax; false declarations expose managers to criminal penalties and ETA administrative seizure. Persistent non-filing does not directly initiate strike-off, but it blocks issuance of tax clearance and therefore prevents renewal of the operating license and commercial registry status.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual partners' meeting resolution approving the audited financial statements and filing of audited accounts in the company's statutory file
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) - Companies Registry / Compliance Department
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The partners' meeting must be convened within six months of fiscal year-end; audited financial statements must be filed with GAFI within 30 days of approval, and in all cases no later than 31 July for a 31 December fiscal year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene the meeting or file the audited accounts constitutes a Companies Law 159/1981 violation; GAFI may impose administrative fines on managers, suspend new activities, and after three consecutive non-filing years commence administrative dissolution proceedings against the LLC.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Retail Commercial License Renewal for grocery store operations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent District Municipality and the Governorate Commercial Licenses Committee
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Before the license anniversary date, and no later than 31 December of the applicable annual licensing cycle; renewal requires a valid tax clearance and civil defence certificate.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Operating without a renewed license exposes the shop to closure orders, daily or fixed administrative penalties, and seizure of non-compliant goods; a license lapsed for more than 12 months triggers cancellation of the operating permit and the commercial registry file is flagged for administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Commercial Registry periodic data confirmation and renewal quota payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: GAFI One-Stop-Shop and the local Commercial Registry Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on the company's registration anniversary, with full re-registration and quota renewal no later than five years from initial registration; updated confirmation must be filed within 30 days of any annual partner or quota transfer change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Overdue renewal quotas accrue administrative surcharges; after 60 days from the renewal due date the Registry may notify the company of intention to strike off. If not cured within a further 90 days, the commercial registration file is cancelled and administrative dissolution is published in the Official Gazette.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No turnover or asset threshold applies. Every Egyptian limited liability company registered under Companies Law 159/1981 must appoint at least one external auditor licensed by the Financial Regulatory Authority / Egyptian Society of Accountants and Auditors, regardless of revenue, employee count, or balance sheet size.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS), which are converged with IFRS; where required by GAFI or the Egyptian Financial Regulatory Authority, listed or licensed entities apply IFRS directly. Statutory books must be kept in Arabic and the financial statements prepared under the Commercial Books Law No. 51 of 1941.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Egyptian AML Law No. 80/2002 and its executive regulations, an LLC must identify and verify the ultimate beneficial owner of each quota holder. There is no standalone annual UBO filing for a private LLC where no transfer has occurred. Instead, on any share/quota transfer the managers must update the quota-holder register and file the change with the commercial registry within 30 days. At the annual partners' meeting approving the financial statements, the managers must certify the register and the UBO schedule, and the on-site documentation must remain available for inspection by GAFI and the Egyptian Financial Intelligence Unit.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of the Partners' General Assembly
Commercial Books (Journal, Ledger, Cash Book, Inventory Book)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300 - USD 1,200 per annum for a small retail LLC in Cairo or Giza using a registered-agent and corporate secretarial package; provincial locations generally range from USD 150 - USD 500 per annum.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 800 - USD 2,500 per annum for a single-branch SME supermarket grocery LLC with orderly cash-based records; multi-branch or related-party operations typically require USD 4,000 - USD 8,000 per annum.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 22.5% on net taxable income (Law 91/2005, Art. 51, as amended by Law 75/2015); no separate municipal corporate profit tax for onshore retail entities
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Optional SME consolidated regime under Law 152/2020: micro enterprises (annual gross revenues up to EGP 1,000,000) taxed at 0.5% of gross revenues; small enterprises (EGP 1,000,000 to EGP 10,000,000) taxed at 1% of gross revenues for retail trade; Investment Law 72/2017 incentives (up to 50% deduction of investment costs in qualifying regions) are generally not available for pure supermarket retailing; no statutory tax holidays for standard onshore retail LLCs

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: ETA Corporate Income Tax Return (Form No. 2) for juridical persons; filed electronically via the Egyptian Tax Authority e-filing portal (eta.gov.eg) using the ETA e-tax system and the taxpayer's unified tax card credential
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within four months after the end of the fiscal year; for a 31 December fiscal year-end the annual return is due by 30 April; provisional income taxes are payable in advance during the year in accordance with ETA quarterly certificate schedules

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification: legal name, Egyptian tax card number, address, registration and incorporation certificate data
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident entity acting through an Egyptian PE must attach the PE tax card and local tax representative authorization; no foreign registration number accepted

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross sales and receipts from supermarket operations, including all POS cash, credit card and electronic payment settlements
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only Egyptian-source retail revenue of the PE is reported; intercompany sales to the foreign head office are excluded and disclosed on the TP annex

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of goods sold: imported Asian condiments, packaged food, fresh vegetables and dry goods, computed from audited stock records
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Imported product costs must be supported by customs entry documents; related-party import prices are adjustable at arm's length

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating expenses: rent, salaries, utility charges, depreciation, freight and store-level overheads
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Head-office cost allocations are deductible only when directly related to the Egyptian PE and substantiated by invoices

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-deductible items add-back: entertainment without supporting documentation, unlicensed donations, reserves and provisions, tax payments, and interest exceeding thin-capitalization limits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add-backs are mandatory even where the same expense is deductible in the home jurisdiction of the foreign shareholder

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax loss carryforward offset: losses absorbed from the previous five years of operations only
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Egyptian PE losses may not be offset against the global profits of the foreign resident shareholder

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after adjustments and final CIT computation at 22.5%, or at the SME gross-revenue rate if validly elected under Law 152/2020
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: PE-attributable profit is taxed at the standard corporate rate without distinction as to foreign ownership

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits for provisional tax payments and withheld taxes, plus declaration of dividend distributions and the 10% dividend withholding tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders may invoke treaty relief at source only after ETA approval of the DTA application package

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Monthly delay surcharge of 6% of unpaid tax for each month of late payment; fixed late-filing fine of EGP 500 to EGP 3,000 per incident; failure to file after ETA reminders triggers discretionary assessment plus an additional margin surcharge of 25% of the assessed tax; criminal liability attaches to the statutory officer for continued non-compliance

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% final withholding tax on cash and in-kind dividend distributions made by Egyptian LLCs to resident and non-resident shareholders (Law 91/2005, Art. 5, as amended by Law 83/2015); the tax is levied at the source on the gross distribution without imputation credit
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident beneficial owner must file with the ETA International Taxation Department before distribution: (i) a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the residence-state tax authority for the relevant fiscal year; (ii) the ETA treaty-relief application and beneficial ownership declaration; (iii) evidence of shareholding percentage; and (iv) confirmation that the dividend income is not attributable to an Egyptian PE. ETA approval grants the reduced treaty rate at source; without prior approval the 10% domestic rate applies and recovery is effected by a refund claim within the five-year statutory claim period. TRC validity is twelve months and, for certain treaty partners, legalization or apostille is required
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties paid to non-residents: 20% statutory withholding under the Law 91/2005 WHT framework, reduced to 10% to 15% under most Egyptian income tax treaties, with trademark royalties frequently capped at a higher residual rate. Interest paid by an Egyptian borrower to a non-resident lender: 20% statutory withholding, typically reduced to 10% or 15% under DTA provisions; the arm's-length interest principle and thin-capitalization limits apply before treaty reduction

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Contemporaneous Local File and Master File are mandatory where aggregate controlled transactions with any single related party exceed EGP 30,000,000 per fiscal year; simplified TP documentation and disclosure through the TP Information Form attached to the annual CIT return are required where controlled transactions with a related party exceed EGP 6,000,000 annually
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP - Comparable Uncontrolled Price (preferred for imported commodity products with public customs or market comparables)
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Egypt has not enacted UAE-style standalone Economic Substance Regulations (ESR), but economic substance is enforced through the GAAR in Law 91/2005, Art. 59, place-of-effective-management analysis, PE deconstruction practices, deemed-profit estimation powers, and anti-conduit interpretations in treaty application; the Asian supermarket must evidence operational substance through physical store premises, committed personnel, POS sales records, audited stock holdings, Egyptian bank accounts, and local management autonomy in order to survive ETA substance review and tax-treaty benefit audits

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion by Concealment or False Records
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Under-declaring POS sales, maintaining dual cash books, fabricating supplier invoices, inflating imported goods costs, or suppressing credit card settlement records related to grocery turnover
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Imprisonment up to five years and fines of EGP 10,000 to EGP 50,000 together with recovery of evaded tax under Law 91/2005; administrative surcharge of 6% per month on the concealed tax; statute of limitations extended to ten years for fraudulent assessments
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and general managers who sign false declarations face criminal prosecution, personal civil liability for evaded tax and surcharges, attachment of personal assets, travel bans, and blocking of outward remittances by ETA enforcement order

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining an Egyptian LLC with no physical store, no employees, no cash register or inventory records, and no local decision-making, while profits are transferred to foreign affiliated entities through artificial procurement or service contracts
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ETA disregard of the corporate form under the GAAR, retroactive deemed-profit assessment at 22.5% CIT, monthly 6% delay surcharge, fines of EGP 5,000 to EGP 20,000 for non-maintenance of accounting books, and revocation of the commercial registry license
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Individuals named as officers may be personally enforced for corporate tax debt through civil attachment; courts have imposed asset freezes and immigration watchlist measures; nominee directors face criminal liability for false attestation in commercial registration filings

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the supermarket POS as an informal money remittance channel for Asian expatriate workers, accepting unexplained high-value cash deposits without customer due diligence, or structuring cash flows through grocery receipts to obscure the source of funds
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines of up to EGP 100,000 per violation under AML Law 80/2002 as amended; EY and Financial Intelligence Unit freezing orders; imprisonment of one to seven years where money-laundering predicates are established; cancellation of the grocery retail license
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers are exposed to criminal prosecution even when the LLC is the facilitation instrument; travel bans are routinely imposed during FIU investigations; confiscation of proceeds and laundering instruments may reach personal assets of the officers

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Documentation Failure / Dividend WHT Avoidance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Setting intra-group import prices for Asian condiments above arm's length to shift Egyptian profit offshore; failing to prepare the TP disclosure form despite threshold breaches; disguising profit distributions as management fees, intercompany loans, or technical assistance fees to avoid the 10% dividend withholding tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Upward TP adjustment to the arm's-length result with an additional margin penalty of 25% of the adjustment; disallowance of disguised fees and interest; application of the 20% withholding framework on recharacterized distributions; fines for non-filing of the TP Information Form up to EGP 50,000
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Officers who execute circular intercompany documentation are jointly liable for the withheld dividend tax, recharacterization assessments, and surcharges; evidence of intentional fee circularization supports prosecutions for tax evasion; statutory representatives may be barred from holding tax clearance certificates, thereby freezing access to banking facilities and procurement contracts
